scoring_justification: Recompute dB2D/dT and dB2D*/dT at 300 K from CSV data via central finite differences and compare hydrogenation-induced slope differences to paper-reported values; recompute anharmonicity from JSON and compare to paper values.

outputs.description: Temperature-dependent thermodynamic properties for pristine silicene from 0 K to 600 K.
Temperature-dependent thermodynamic properties for hydrogenated silicene from 0 K to 600 K.
Temperature-dependent thermodynamic properties for germanene from 0 K to 600 K.
Temperature-dependent thermodynamic properties for hydrogenated germanene from 0 K to 600 K.
Equilibrium anharmonicity measure a·dB2D_star/da for the four systems.

output_contract.notes: The hidden checker recomputes temperature derivatives at 300 K from the CSV data (using central differences) and compares them to reference values with appropriate tolerances; it also compares the anharmonicity coefficients to reference values. Each CSV must contain at least 20 temperature points covering 0–600 K. Shape and completeness are part of the scoring.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold values for slope differences and anharmonicity coefficients
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text: Si to HSi B2D increase 5.0e-5 eV/Å^2/K; Ge to HGe net increase 2.4e-5 eV/Å^2/K. Anharmonicity: Si -6.3, HSi -13.3, Ge -18.6, HGe -13.8 eV/Å^2.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the paper's reported numbers (Sec. III, Table I, and text).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values are directly the paper's reported coefficients and slope changes; no synthetic data.

steps.description: Verify Si CSV has required columns and at least 20 temperature points covering 0–600 K.
Verify HSi CSV has required columns and at least 20 temperature points covering 0–600 K.
Verify Ge CSV has required columns and at least 20 temperature points covering 0–600 K.
Verify HGe CSV has required columns and at least 20 temperature points covering 0–600 K.
Compute dB2D/dT and dB2D*/dT at 300 K from all CSVs; compare hydrogenation-induced changes to paper gold.
Compare anharmonicity coefficients to paper values within ±2 eV/Å^2.
